key_insight: VideoDetective jointly reasons about extrinsic query-to-segment relevance and intrinsic inter-segment affinity to identify sparse, high-value clips from very long videos, enabling multimodal LLMs to answer queries with limited context windows more accurately and efficiently.
problem_solved: Enables accurate query-driven understanding of long videos by locating sparse, relevant segments while accounting for the video's internal structure and varying segment relevance—overcoming context-window and localization limits in current MLLM pipelines.
method: Compute extrinsic relevance: score each video segment against the input query to capture direct clue signals.
Model intrinsic affinity: build inter-segment relationships (affinity graph) to propagate relevance and reveal contextually important clips beyond direct query matches.
Fuse relevance + affinity to sparsely select and assemble the most informative clips for downstream MLLM reasoning, reducing context load and improving answer quality.
impact: Makes long-video QA, retrieval, and summarization scalable to real-world lengths by improving accuracy with far fewer input tokens and providing interpretable clip-level evidence—practical for deployment where compute and context are limited.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: query -> extrinsic scoring + intrinsic affinity -> fusion -> selected clips -> MLLM
Timeline heatmap: video timeline with color-coded relevance and propagated affinity highlights
Affinity graph inset: nodes=segments, edges=affinity scores showing propagation of relevance
Before/after bar chart: accuracy or token usage comparison vs. query-only baselines
paper_title: VideoDetective: Clue Hunting via both Extrinsic Query and Intrinsic Relevance for Long Video Understanding
paper_authors: Ruoliu Yang, Chu Wu, Caifeng Shan, Ran He, Chaoyou Fu
